items.title: Mercury is the only metal you can pour at room temperature
items.claim: Cadmium melts at 321°C, zinc at 420°C, gold at 1064°C. Mercury melts at -39°C. Sit it in your hand and you watch a metal flow.

options.text: Mercury is not really a metal

Relativistic contraction of mercury's 6s orbital means its outer electrons resist delocalising into the metallic 'sea'; mercury atoms are held together more by weak van der Waals forces than by strong metallic bonding, so the lattice melts at low temperature
Mercury atoms are too heavy to form a solid
Mercury contains hidden noble gas atoms

items.reveal:
Mercury's atomic configuration is [Xe] 4f14 5d10 6s2. The 6s electrons are relativistically contracted (a consequence of inner electrons moving at relativistic speeds in a high-Z element), making them behave more like a closed shell than typical valence electrons.

Metallic bonding relies on delocalised valence electrons. Mercury's 6s pair is reluctant to delocalise, so Hg-Hg bonds are weak. Calculations suggest that without relativistic effects, mercury would melt around 80°C — much like cadmium.

Mercury thermometers, dental amalgams and gold extraction all depend on this anomalous liquidity.
items.why: Mercury's familiar behaviour is one of the most everyday consequences of special relativity.

items.title: Going down a group does NOT always mean smaller ionisation energy
items.claim: First ionisation energies generally decrease down a group as the outer electron sits in a larger, more shielded orbital. Yet gold's first IE (890 kJ/mol) is HIGHER than silver's (731), and silver is higher than copper's (745) is debatable.
items.prompt: Why do the textbook trends break down here?

options.text: Relativistic contraction of the 6s orbital in heavy elements (gold, mercury) lowers the outer electron's energy, making it more tightly bound than a non-relativistic shielding picture would predict
Gold is not really in Group 11
Outer electrons of gold are pulled by nuclear charge alone

items.reveal:
Simple shielding arguments predict each row's outer electron should be easier to remove than the row above. They work moderately well for s-block and p-block. They fail for heavy transition metals and post-transition metals where relativistic effects matter.

Gold's 6s orbital contracts and becomes more 'core-like'. Its first ionisation energy rises. Mercury is similar.

Another counter-trend: across a period, IE generally rises, but boron < beryllium (because B's outer electron is in a higher-energy 2p, while Be's is in the lower 2s); oxygen < nitrogen (pairing penalty in O's half-filled 2p4 vs N's stable 2p3 half-filled).
items.why: Periodic trends are taught as smooth ladders. Real data has dips and bumps that diagnose deeper physics.

items.title: Two molecules with identical formulas, opposite effects
items.claim: Thalidomide was sold in the 1950s as a sedative and anti-nausea drug for pregnant women. The molecule has a single chiral centre. One enantiomer treats morning sickness. The other causes catastrophic birth defects.
items.prompt: Why couldn't doctors simply sell the 'safe' enantiomer?

options.text: The safe enantiomer is too expensive to purify
Thalidomide racemises in the body — even if you give pure (R)-thalidomide, the body converts some to the harmful (S) form
Doctors did sell the safe one — the thalidomide disaster never actually happened

items.reveal:
Receptors in the body are chiral. They distinguish enantiomers the way a left hand distinguishes a left glove from a right glove. The (R) enantiomer of thalidomide sedates; the (S) enantiomer binds to a different protein involved in limb development.

The critical complication: thalidomide racemises in vivo. The chiral centre is alpha to a carbonyl, and the proton there can be lost and re-added on either face. So even pure (R)-thalidomide becomes a racemic mixture inside the body within hours.

Modern pharma uses chiral synthesis and tests both enantiomers for activity AND for unintended effects.
items.why: Two molecules with the same atoms in the same order can behave like medicine and poison. Stereochemistry is consequential.
